provenance.notes: hash_ids and present_ids transcribed from the test's own ASSERT_EQ vectors.
The only upstream vector that reaches the negative-remainder correction and the sign path of the wrapping multiply; transcribed from its ASSERT_EQ.
First chunk of the chained run; its hash ids are the first eight entries of the full-sequence ASSERT_EQ vector.
Decode step fed the previous call's present_ids; its hash ids are entries 8..11 of the full-sequence ASSERT_EQ vector.
Last decode step of the chain; its hash ids are entries 12..15 of the full-sequence ASSERT_EQ vector and its present_ids match the full run.
No new tokens: hash_ids is empty and the window passes through unchanged.
The upstream batched geometry and inputs; expected values recomputed from the CPU kernel's algorithm because upstream builds them with its in-file reference rather than an ASSERT_EQ table.

Upstream's CPU kernel rejects a non-positive vocabulary size; every GPU implementation guards the division and emits 0 for that head, and only the guarded behaviour is reachable here. Head 2 is the invalid one.
A single head per n-gram order, so two hash ids per position; seven positions leave a tail inside the last tile.
One head per order with a carry state and two batch rows, including a negative history id and a negative pad.
A wider Engram configuration: three n-gram orders times four heads is twelve hash ids per position.
Two new tokens against a three-slot window, so one present slot still comes from past_ids and the deepest shift reads history for both positions.
The smallest legal configuration: one n-gram order, one head, a one-slot window.
One head across four n-gram orders, so three hash ids per position over two batch rows.
Every product here overflows 32 bits, so the two's-complement wrap is what produces these values; an int64 run of the same inputs would wrap at 64 bits and disagree.
The int32 boundary values as ids, multipliers, history and pad, where the wrapping multiply and the negative-remainder correction meet.
1027 positions spill past the first workgroup tile and leave a partial tile, over ids that sweep through negative and positive values so the remainder correction runs at scale.
Four batch rows of 600 positions: one workgroup row per batch row, several span tiles each, with a carry state per row.
One span slot per invocation and a 64-invocation workgroup, so the tile walk runs with the smallest rendered tile and every tile boundary is crossed.
2500 positions at the default tile width, so the middle tile is wholly interior: every slot in it hashes a token whose window lies inside the sequence, and the leading and trailing tiles are not.
Two batch rows of 2,200 positions with carry state check history-dependent output across a long sequence.
A 64-slot tile, so an interior tile occurs well before the end of a 300-position sequence.
